task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a reported feature of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the dawn porters who prepare Harrow Quay's produce market. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Harrow Quay produce market uses a five-person paid porter crew to move deliveries from its loading edge to traders' pitches before opening.
The crew is employed through the traders' joint service agreement, not organized as an unpaid volunteer group.
In the supplied morning scene, crew leader Daro Venn checks chalked pitch numbers as the first vegetable truck reaches the loading edge at 4:45 a.m.
The porters use wheeled carts through lanes that must be clear of delivery vehicles before customers enter.
The current arrangement ends routine vehicle unloading at 7:30 a.m., while the public market opens at 9 a.m.
Venn said, "You learn the sound of the carts. A loose wheel announces itself before the trader comes looking for it."
A late truck can affect several stalls because the crew shares carts and access lanes rather than working as five independent delivery services.
The crew records damaged carts and broken paving through the market manager's maintenance log.
The porter agreement covers movement within the market, not the condition of produce before it arrives or every trader's road transport.
Fruit trader Selma Rill lays out empty trays while her delivered crates wait at the marked unloading point.
Rill said, "If I spend the first hour chasing boxes, I have not spent it getting ready for the people who buy from me."
Traders contribute to the shared porter service through the market's published operating charge.
The packet does not disclose the crew's individual pay rates or calculate a monetary value for time saved by each stall.
The market manager has asked suppliers to give notice of unusual loads because a standard cart is not suitable for every delivery.
New porters spend their first shifts alongside an experienced worker to learn pitch locations and the shared-lane routine.
The supplied scene describes the market gradually changing from stacks of closed crates to signs, price cards and open customer aisles.
The same lanes are used for waste removal after closing, under a separately timed part of the market's daily operation.
The market's older pitch names remain in everyday speech even where the current plan uses numbered positions.
A planned paving repair will require a temporary unloading arrangement, but the manager has not announced a change in public opening hours.
The crew keeps a kettle in a small room beside the cart store and takes breaks according to the delivery sequence.
The packet describes one supplied morning and the standing work arrangement, not a measured account of every market day's workload.
The traders have retained the shared service for the coming season rather than shifting all unloading responsibility to individual stallholders.

forbidden_additions: Unpaid volunteer labor, invented pay rates or a measured productivity saving.
Responsibility for all upstream delivery conditions.
One morning generalized into an identical daily workload or changed public opening time.
preserve: The linked work of porters and traders within shared physical constraints.
The transition from unloading to a public market.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
